Amy / Jack — thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we heard from FinHealth:
- Primary concern: strict logical/data isolation for PHI-related calls and model inputs/outputs.
- Preference: unsure between Dedicated capacity (Redwood-managed GPUs with tenant isolation) and Private VPC (Redwood stack deployed into customer VPC / on-prem).
- Key asks: customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM), control-plane residency options, audit log detail & retention, evidence for compliance (SOC2 / pen test), and a clear POC timeline.

Open questions (please confirm):
1) Is BYOK via customer KMS required for both encryption at rest and for KV cache encryption?
2) Do you require the Redwood control plane to sit inside your VPC (private control plane) or is a hosted control plane acceptable provided data plane lives in your VPC?
3) Minimum audit log retention window and format (SIEM-friendly syslog/JSON?).

Proposed next steps:
- I can assemble a short evidence packet (SOC2 summary + architecture sketch + checklist) — attaching SOC2_report_redwood_2025.pdf and deployment-options-one-pager.pdf.
- Technical deep-dive with Marissa and your infra/security folks week of Oct 4 — suggested slot: Tue Oct 6, 10:00am PT.
- If you want to proceed with a POC, we can provision a private VPC POC or a dedicated-reserved pool depending on your preference; we recommend private VPC for the strictest custody guarantees.

Please confirm the items above and the Oct 6 time, and flag any follow-up items to add.

Thanks —

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Our security team’s current leaning is toward Private VPC because we need full network egress controls and the ability to restrict control-plane traffic to known management subnets. If the control plane can be placed in our VPC or we can run the entire control plane privately, that would be preferred.
- BYOK is a hard requirement for encryption at rest for any PHI-related workloads; we also want to confirm whether Redwood supports HSM-backed keys in our KMS.
- Audit logs: we need at least 2 years retention and the ability to export logs in JSON to our SIEM.

We’d like Marissa and your security lead on a short technical call. Oct 6 10:00am PT should work — please send a calendar invite and any pre-read. I’ll ask our infra folks to join as well.

Ben / Rishi / Amy — thanks, looping in a short tech note ahead of our call. High level:

1) Control plane options
- Hosted control plane (default): control APIs run in Redwood’s control plane. Customer data plane (inference nodes / KV cache) can be deployed inside a customer VPC, ensuring payloads never transit public networks.
- Private control plane: we can deploy a private control plane into customer VPCs for higher assurance; this requires an onboarding window (~3-4 weeks) and additional ops runbook (we’ll include an SLO/patching plan).

2) BYOK / KMS / HSM
- We support customer-managed KMS across supported cloud providers (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK). HSM-backed keys supported where customer KMS provides them (we integrate via CMEK APIs).
- For KV cache encryption we can enable CMEK; per-POD keys are configurable for the POC.

3) Audit logs & retention
- We can stream audit logs (JSON) to a customer syslog endpoint or S3 bucket; typical retention in our internal system is 90 days but streaming to the customer gives them full control for multi-year retention.

4) POC proposition
- Recommended: Private VPC POC with customer-managed KMS + optional private control plane. Deliverables: architecture diagram (attached: pvn-arch-v1.png), pre-read checklist (networks, subnets, IAM, certs), and a scoped timeline: kickoff -> infra prep (1 week) -> deployment & validation (1 week) -> joint tests (1 week).

Attachments: pvn-arch-v1.png

I’ll be on the Oct 6 call to walk the architecture and confirm the onboarding steps. If FinHealth wants a dedicated-reserved pool instead, that’s doable but it removes the customer KMS option unless we do a private VPC path.

—Marissa
